items.statement: Expects gradual margin improvement over next 2-3 quarters; no number given.

items.statement: Europe automotive decision-making delayed; deals in final shortlist not signed, timing uncertain.

items.statement: JLR going through challenges including layoffs; monitoring closely in H2.

items.statement: Onsite-offshore revenue mix roughly 25:75, considered a good band.

items.statement: Project finance loans to start commercial operations in 6-9 months.

items.quote: This year looks difficult because we are waiting for the approval.

items.statement: Focus remains on delivering sustainable VNB growth, balancing growth, profitability, risk and prudence; protection and annuity stay central.
items.quote: Our strategy remains unchanged, delivering sustainable VNB growth while balancing business growth, profitability, and risk and prudence. Protection and annuity stay central to our strategy, addressing significant underpenetrated needs in India.

items.statement: Retail protection growth expected to taper in H2 from 40-50% levels to more moderate levels.
items.quote: The expectation is that as you get into H2 of this year, those growth numbers should taper down from the 40%-50% that we've been seeing to more moderate levels.

items.statement: Par to non-par mix in last quarter broadly in the range of 60:40.

items.statement: VNB margin expansion from FY2026 to H1 FY2027 largely explained by product mix shift.

items.statement: Company repriced non-par products as a continuous exercise based on market yields.

items.statement: Improved profitability from yields and opex is passed on to customers via better pricing to propel demand.

items.statement: If rates stay high longer, non-par and annuity can become a larger proportion of business.
items.quote: If the rates stay high for longer, then it is likely that non-par as a share, and this also adds annuity to it, both of these can become a larger proportion of the business, not just for us, for others as well.

items.statement: Annuity and guaranteed products attractive in IRRs and have done well across all distribution channels.
items.quote: These products are very attractive in terms of IRRs, both the annuities, which have been on the regular pay variety, as well as the guaranteed products, which also are both income as well as lump sum variety. And they've done quite well across all of our distribution channels.

items.statement: Consultation paper on distribution economics is early; regulator collecting feedback, no closure yet.
items.quote: I think it's a consultation paper at this point. It's not a draft regulation. items.statement: Too early to call volume impact from proposed commission structure changes; renewal commission space provides comfort.
items.quote: It's too difficult to call, Swarnabha. The way you also look at this is that there is sufficient space that the regulator has set out in terms of renewal commission.

items.statement: Operating expenses excluding GST and stamp duty reduced at 8% CAGR over last three years.

items.statement: Company comfortable with IFRS and RBC numbers; strategy unchanged under new standards.
items.quote: We're comfortable with the way that the IFRS numbers are stacking up. We're comfortable with RBC.

items.statement: Agency channel to continue receiving investment; gross agent additions grew 23% in half-year.
items.quote: I think the opex advantage that we have allows us to continue to invest in Agency. And even when you look at this half-year, in terms of the gross addition of agents, that's 23% growth, which is ahead of the rest of the market.

items.statement: Company does not provide growth guidance; focus on medium-term sustainable growth.
items.quote: Again, we don't provide guidance. We can give you what we should look at from the medium term.

items.statement: October trends too early to call, only 10-12 days into the quarter.
items.quote: October too early to call. It's just been about 10-12 days, too early in the quarter to call this out.

items.statement: Credit life growth in line with protection growth; wide diversity of partners including parent bank.
items.quote: So the growth in credit life has been quite in line with what you're seeing in the protection growth for this quarter as well. So, it's a fairly decent growth that we're seeing at this point.

items.statement: Full-year FY27 ESOP non-cash expense expected around INR79-80 crores.
items.quote: Yes. So the noncash expense for ESOP cost for the full year FY '27 would be around INR79 crores, INR80 crores.

items.statement: AIF fees are 80-90 bps, above mutual fund equity book; discretionary PMS similar to equity MF; non-discretionary PMS strategic; government mandates highly contested.
items.quote: On the margins question, AIF is a margin-accretive business. Fees here sit above what we earn on our mutual fund equity book in the range of 80 to 90 basis points depending on the product.

items.statement: SIF product launches expected over next couple of quarters.
items.quote: We are now well set, and you will see a couple of product launches in this space over the next couple of quarters.

items.statement: Costs split into inflation-linked routine expenses and upfront investments in people, technology, distribution.
items.quote: So I mentioned, I think it's split into two. items.statement: Alternative investment team has over 20 professionals, expanding investor servicing, operations, sales, distribution.
items.quote: So between alternative and PMS, when I say alternative, both private equity and private credit, we've got more than 20 investment professionals now and significantly expanding our capacity on investor servicing, on operations, on the whole sales and then the distribution side, so on and so forth.

items.statement: Mutual fund investment team grew from 30 to nearly 40 professionals and will continue to grow.
items.quote: But even on the mutual fund side, team till a couple of years back was like 30 professionals. Now number is like closer to 40, and this will continue to grow.

items.statement: Investing upfront in international business despite small AUM due to potential.
items.quote: Same thing is on the international side, where the AUM is not very large, but we are investing upfront because we see a lot of potential in that business.

items.statement: Investing in AI-led capabilities across major business functions with upfront costs and future benefits.
items.quote: And then, of course, the technology where a team of engineers working on AI-led capabilities across major business functions. So this is like upfront investments, but in terms of the cost saving, potential cost saving or the potential higher revenues will occur over a period of time.

items.statement: Board distributed almost all post-tax cash profits as dividend; balance sheet used for seed capital in alternate platforms.
items.quote: For the last year, the Board ha s declared a dividend, which effectively where we have distributed the almost entire post-tax cash profits that we generate. The balance sheet that we have, currently, we are using for seed capital for all our alternate platforms.

items.statement: Seeding new strategies requires ongoing seed capital.
items.quote: It is a continuing process. As we keep seeding new strategies, this will require seed capital.

items.statement: H1 cost skewed by CSR expenses in Q1; request to look at full-year expenses.
items.quote: Sir, actually, we had mentioned this in our last quarterly call. There were some CSR expenses which were taken up in the first quarter. And because of that, you are seeing the H1 numbers getting kind of a bit skewed.

items.statement: SIP market share increased when excluding STP; systematic transactions rose from 17 million in June to nearly 19 million in September.
items.quote: If you strip out STP and look at SIP alone, our market share has actually gone up. I repeat. If you strip out STP and look at only the SIP, our market share has actually gone up.

items.statement: Monthly systematic transaction book grew nearly 5x in 5 years to around INR48 billion; industry grew 3x.
items.quote: And if we step back for a moment, monthly systematic transaction book has grown nearly 5x in about 5 years to around INR48 billion and industry in the same p eriod would have grown 3x.

items.statement: Small cap fund remains 0.5% of small-cap universe market cap, same as June 2019.
items.quote: So if you look at, for example, the small cap fund and some of the people have heard saying that now it's INR40,000 crores. But it was 0.5% of the small-cap universe market cap in June '19, if I remember correctly. And it's still like 0.5% of the market cap universe today.

items.statement: Weighted average market cap of mid and small cap funds below category average.
items.quote: And also the other thing that we constantly look at both for our mid-cap fund and small-cap fund is the weighted average market cap of that fund vis-a-vis the benchmark and vis -a-vis the category average. And our weighted average market cap in that sits below the category average.

items.statement: Launched two outbound funds in GIFT City; six inbound funds; will keep evaluating product bouquet.
items.quote: Yes, so continuously been expanding the product bouquet. We have got six funds for inbound investment that is investment by global investors in India. And recently, we have launched two products for outbound where there's an opportunity for Indian investors to invest globally.

items.statement: Targets $600-650 million UBS flow exchange by March end, with $300-325 million already done.
items.quote: I think onboarding has got initiated. So, in some senses, we've internally looked at a target of exchanging $600 odd million in flows for the current financial year.

items.statement: Expects 100-150 bps cost-to-income improvement year-on-year.
items.quote: I think we had guided for a 1 - 1.5% kind of overall improvement year-on-year. I think we are well on course to achieve that.

items.statement: Targets doubling profits over 3.5 years, no need to raise capital, aiming for 20% ROE.

items.statement: Expects equity brokerage to grow from ₹8-9 crores to ₹15-20 crores per month.

items.statement: Expects TBR to grow to ₹800-1,000 crores when revenue reaches ₹5,000-5,500 crores.

items.statement: Expects 40-50 bps retention on UBS flows both ways.
items.quote: I think it’s safe to assume 40 - 50 basis points of retention would broadly come through.

items.statement: Expects ₹3,000-3,500 crores fund redemption over next 6-18 months, hopes most money returns.
items.quote: I think, yes, that fund will go back over the space of next 6 - 18 months. So, that’s the only large fund, I think, which is up for redemption, which is around about ₹3,000 - 3,500 crores.

items.statement: Expects cost-to-income ratio to stay within 100-200 bps as new hires are added.
items.quote: But overall, all three things put together, I think we should be able to kind of keep it within the 100 - 200 basis points cost to income ratio as we build it out.

items.statement: Expects asset management flows to meet targets for current year.
items.quote: I think flows will kind of come back and overall should be in a position to meet our targets for the current year.

items.statement: Expects HNI business to break even on direct costs soon.
items.quote: With productivity improving and a growing feeder pipeline into UHNI, we expect the business to break even on direct costs soon.

items.statement: Expects 18-20% ROE over 3-3.5 years on tangible net worth.
items.quote: I think we definitely would aim to, over a period of 3 - 3.5 years, ensure that we are around that 20% zip code on the tangible net worth.

items.statement: Expects 50% of flows from wallet share and 50% from new mandates going forward.

items.statement: Expects 1:2 split of net flows from new clients and existing clients.
items.quote: I think largely we look at 1:2 split, 1/3 rd from new clients and 2/3rd from existing clients.

items.statement: Expects 65-72-73 bps overall retention on large mandates.
items.quote: But I think if I look at the relationship, overall, I think we are coming back to the same 65 - 72 - 73 basis points overall.

items.statement: Employee cost guidance of about ₹1,100 crores including ESOP cost for FY27, flat year-on-year
items.quote: So we'll continue to maintain our guidance of about ₹ 1,100 crores of employee costs, including the cost of stock options for this financial year, which is flat for year-on-year comparison.

items.quote: In September, average daily orders rebounded to 5.8 million, up nearly 12% from August.

items.quote: Gross broking income now accounts for approximately 55% of total revenues compared with nearly 60% a year ago.

items.quote: In September, we delivered our highest ever credit distribution, taking our annualized run rate to ₹ 33 billion.

items.quote: We have received authorization to operate as a Global Access Provider in the IFSC. With that, we are piloting U.S. stocks on our platform.

items.statement: MTF book quality solid: 85%+ in blue chip and good categories; 84% of funded clients have exposure below ₹100,000; 82% of book less than 30 days old; delinquencies negligible
items.quote: Largely, our book is good and blue chip constitutes almost upwards of 85%.

items.statement: New business burn (drag on EBITDA margin) at 3.5% to 4%, up from 2.5%-3% six quarters ago
items.quote: So that burn is about 3.5% to 4%, as I mentioned in the previous call also. So it remains in that range.

items.statement: Brand spend as percentage of revenue expected to decline over time as revenue scales while spend stays flat
items.quote: You should expect that over a period of time as a percentage of revenue, definitely, the spends will come down unless we sort of see a new opportunity.

items.quote: The joint venture envisages setting up two advanced pipe manufacturing facilities, helical pipes and longitudinal pipes with a capacity of 300,000 metric ton each, catering to the region's growing water infrastructure and energy requirement.

items.statement: Geopolitical tensions in West Asia causing shipping delays and revenue recognition delays.
items.quote: Ongoing geopolitical tension in West Asia have worsened due to recent escalation s in Saudi Arabia, a region where we hold significant export order exposure. The main challenge is not other order cancellation, but rather delay in shipping and revenue recognition.

items.statement: Abu Dhabi DI plant facing cost overrun, underutilization, and delivery constraints.
items.quote: The Abu Dhabi DI plant is facing a combination of cost overrun, underutilization, and delivery constraints, including difficulties serving customers who cannot be reached through truck-based transportation.

items.statement: Domestic water business softness continues, impacting capacity utilization.
items.quote: This pressure was further compounded by lower capacity utilization due to lower execution in water pipe business as softness in domestic water business continues.

items.statement: Surging raw material costs, particularly coking coal, squeezed DI pipe margins.
items.quote: Surging raw material costs, particularly for coking coal have squeezed margins in the DI pipe business.

items.statement: New orders from oil and gas and exports to change product mix and improve margins.
items.quote: And we are seeing that from Q3 onwards, we may see some upward trend in terms of margins also because this new orders will change the product mix in the time to come. Because the majority of the orders are coming from the oil and gas sector and exports.

items.statement: Anti-dumping duty on Indian DI pipe exports to Saudi Arabia not impacting company as it exports via Abu Dhabi.
items.quote: However, the other manufacturers in India, the duty is being imposed on them in the range of 16 % to 25% to 30%, based on the -- their export to this region and their pricing. So, that is something which is positive for us that we are not included in the anti-dumping duty liability.

items.statement: Saudi DI pipe project put on hold; will serve market from Abu Dhabi.
items.quote: Right now, considering the Saudi scenario, we have put on hold that venture. It in any case was very small.

items.statement: Jindal ITF vs NTPC litigation: next hearing scheduled for January 2027.
items.quote: The next hearing is scheduled for January 2027.

items.statement: Expects mid-double-digit consolidated revenue growth for H2 FY27, around 15%.
items.quote: So in terms of the guidance, we just say that we are looking for mid -double-digit revenue growth, and this can be somewhere around 15% in that range.

items.statement: Expects to maintain minimum EBITDA margin at last year's level.
items.quote: Given continued macroeconomic uncertainty and inflationary environment, but improved execution cycle, we are expecting a medium double-digit consolidated revenue growth for remaining part of the year while maintaining minimum EBITDA margin at last year's level.

items.statement: Guides 20-22% EBIT margin for Gear division.
items.quote: So we could -- we used to always guide to our shareholders that we will maintain 20% to 22% EBIT margin for gear, and we are happy to re port that we are leading towards that trajectory that we always wanted to achieve.

items.statement: Guides 22-24% EBIT margin for MHE division for the year.
items.quote: As far as MHE division is concerned, I think we have given guidance that we will maintain our margin throughout the year that is in the range of 22% to 24%, okay?

items.statement: Gear open order book INR1,056 crores as of Sep 30, 2026, up 37% YoY.
items.quote: The open order book was INR1,056 crores as of September 30, 2026. This is up by 37% year-on-year, providing strong H2 visibility.

items.statement: MHE open order book INR579 crores as of Sep 30, up 27.3% YoY.
items.quote: The open order book reached to INR 579 crores as of September 30, up 27.3% year -on-year. This provides sound execution visibility.

items.statement: MHE secured orders worth approximately USD9 million in H1 FY27.
items.quote: Our MHE division is now establishing a meaningful international presence, securing orders worth approximately USD9 million during the first half.

items.statement: Overseas order inflow in Q2 was INR230 crores.
items.quote: Coming back to the order inflow for the exports, it's about INR230 crores in Q2.

items.statement: Overseas order book outstanding INR326 crores.
items.quote: Yes. So it is INR326 crores.

items.statement: Took price hikes and improved product mix to offset input costs.
items.quote: So we have basically, we have taken a price hike and also a bit of improvement of product mix.

items.statement: Expects momentum to pick up after Diwali, especially till March.
items.quote: But what it looks like is that after Diwali, the expected momentum would catch up for th e near future, okay, especially till March.

items.statement: Sees strong demand from cement, power, steel, fertilizers, and ports for MHE.
items.quote: Execution improved progressively compared with Q1, while demand from steel, power, cement, fertilizers and ports remains supportive.

items.statement: Product mix: 53% catalog, 47% engineered.
items.quote: It's about 53% is catalog, 47% is engineering.

items.statement: Notes volatility in steel prices and inflationary pressures.
items.quote: First of all, I would like to say that there was a lot of volatility in the pricing of steel in the last 6 months, which would affect our margins.

items.statement: Board declared interim dividend of INR0.50 per share.
items.quote: Furthermore, we are pleased that the Board has declared an interim dividend of INR 0.50 per equity share of face value of INR1 each, reaffirming our commitment to delivering value to our shareholders.

items.statement: Capital expenditure program for 3 years remains on track.
items.quote: We also remain committed to our capital expenditure program for 3 years, which remains on track.

items.statement: Bank sticks to 15-16% loan and deposit growth guidance, preferring higher end, around 16%.
items.quote: So in terms of guidance, bank has already given a guidance of 15% to 16% in terms of loans and deposits. I think we would like to stick on to that. But preferably, it will be in the higher bucket of that guidance, what we have given.

items.statement: NIM expected to improve to 3.36-3.38% in shorter term and 3.45-3.50% over 12 months.
items.quote: And of course, in the longer term, our 12 months or 4 quarters guidance will be around 3.45 to 3.50, we should take. So that is what the guidance for NIM.

items.statement: NIM should improve and move towards 3.36 to 3.38 levels in the shorter term.
items.quote: And we believe that this Repo rate what has hiked and the consistent churning what we are doing, the NIM should improve and move towards 3.36 to 3.38 levels in the shorter term.

items.statement: Medium-term ROA target is 1.25% to 1.30%, long-term target 1.5%.
items.quote: And of course, our medium -term target will be to reach 1.2 5% to 1.30%. And obviously, our final -- as a long-term target will be to reach that 1.5% mark.

items.statement: ROA expected to inch up from 1.1% to 1.20-1.25% within a year.
items.quote: I am pretty sure that this is likely to inch up from the 1.1, which we are currently at to 1.20 and 1.25 levels very shortly, maybe in a year itself, we should see that k ind of a movement.

items.statement: Board permitted raising INR500 crores of Tier 2 bonds; no major capital raise expected now.
items.quote: Currently, the Board has permitted us to raise INR500 crores of Tier 2 bonds. And we are currently not expecting a raising of capital at this point of time when we are well capitalized at 19.40.

items.statement: Gold loan share targeted to increase from 25% to 30-32% immediately, eventually 35%.
items.quote: So bank already is targeting to take it up to 35%. So that I will stand by that as a first phase, then let us see how the industry evolves. And then from there, we will take on. B ut at this point of time, the focus will be to take it up to 30%, 32% levels immediately.

items.statement: Retail segment outperforming wholesale; growth in MSME, retail, agri disbursements.
items.quote: The retail segment is currently outperforming the wholesale segment. I can tell you that, that there is a significant amount of push happening and there's growth happening in retail side.

items.statement: Corporate loan yields increased 25-30 bps due to Repo and T-Bill rate upticks.
items.quote: So both the aspects, if you see for the last 3 months, there has been upticks in -- up to the extent of maybe 25 to 30 basis points. So to that extent, the new corporate bookings have started increasing.

items.statement: Repo rate hike passed on to new gold loans, but no spread increase yet.
items.quote: And in terms of gold loan, at this point of time, the Repo price what is there that has been passed on to the new loans, but we have not thought of increasing the spread at this point of time.

items.statement: ECL provisioning impact not substantial due to low SMA and net NPA.
items.quote: It's not very substantial. That much I can say. It is not very substantial because you can see from my balance sheet itself because the SMA numbers are at the lowest, the net NPA numbers are at the lowest.

items.statement: Cost-to-income ratio expected to come down to 50% going forward.
items.quote: I think we are right on that because we should see the cost-to-income ratio coming down to 50%, 50% going forward.

items.statement: Opex growth will be lower than loan growth.
items.quote: It will be -- opex growth will be lower than the loan growth. There will be opex growth, but it will be lower than loan growth.

items.statement: Recovery from technical written-off accounts expected to decline to INR50-55 crores on average.
items.quote: But on an average, we expect that INR50 crores to INR55 crores to continue.

items.statement: Bancassurance income sustainable; recovery from written-off accounts to decline after 4-6 quarters.
items.quote: But over a period of time, maybe after say, 4 to 5 quarters or 6 quarters, this amount is likely to come down because of the nonexistence of the NPA stock.

items.statement: Every basis point hardening in yields results in INR1-1.1 crores MTM impact.
items.quote: And in terms of the rate going up from that 7.19 towards currently at 7.40, and all see, every basis point will result in approximately INR1 crores to INR1.1 crores for us.

items.statement: No change in guidance; on track to meet or exceed 25% AUM growth, similar profit growth, and 20% ROE.
items.quote: So there's no change in guidance as such. But I think, hopefully, we are on track to meet and exceed the guidance. So the guidance there is like 25% AUM growth and similar profit growth and ROE of around -- the upper end of the guidance and ROE is 20%.

items.statement: Committed to raise equity capital at the earliest opportunity, hopefully this quarter, with dilution of 10% to 20%.
items.quote: But one thing is that, that we are committed to raise equity capital at the earliest opportunity. Hopefully, this quarter, we should be able to close something.

items.statement: Home finance AUM growth guidance of 18% to 20%, well within that; ROE target 16% to 18% for next year.
items.quote: We had guided growth of 18% to 20% on AUM, we'll be well within that because we are already at 8% after two quarters.

items.statement: Consolidated ROE to remain above 20% in medium to long term, may be temporarily lower after equity raise.
items.quote: So in the medium to long term, we got to keep it above 20%, that's what our target is.

items.statement: Gold loan market expanding; expect to maintain growth momentum in second half if gold prices stable.
items.quote: I personally think that if the gold prices remain stable. I'm not saying that they will go up even if they remain plus/minus 10% and environment economy remains what it is, then we should be able to maintain our growth momentum.

items.statement: MSME yields lower due to shift to superior quality borrowers; new business yield around 12.5% to 13.5%.
items.quote: Now the new business that we are doing is maybe around 12.5% to 13.5%, but then quality is very superior and the losses are minimal.

items.statement: Home loan boarding yield increased to 11.81% in Q2, expected to pull up portfolio yield over 2-3 quarters.
items.quote: If you see for quarter 2, the yield has gone up to 11.81%, which is much above the portfolio rate. So with every passing quarter, this will pull up the yield.

items.statement: Affordable home loan disbursements doubled to INR790 crores in Q2; added 38 new branches in affordable segment.
items.quote: In Q2, we have disbursed affordable now almost about INR790 crores. In quarter 1, it was about INR400 crores.

items.statement: Insurance commission regulatory impact: HFC and Samasta affected; PBT impact around 5% or less.
items.quote: So it will be at a -- PBT level will be around 5% or so, not 10% for us, maybe a little less than that.

items.statement: Microfinance disbursements to pick up in second half; targeting INR1,000 crores monthly run rate by Feb-March.
items.quote: We should be looking at around 1,000 a month.

items.statement: Gold loan NPAs may spike if gold prices fall suddenly, but ultimate losses negligible due to collateral.
items.quote: So NPAs may vary. They may go up to 1%, 2%, 3% also in such scenario. But ultimate loss will be minimal because most of the time what happens that customers also know that the gold and the jewellery that they pledged the value is significantly higher.

items.statement: Added 38 new branches, total now 350, all in affordable housing segment.
items.quote: On branches, we have added 38 branches, new branches. So we were at about 311, now we are 350. All the branches are in affordable.

items.statement: MSME ROA target 2.5%-3% next year; this year breakeven or slightly positive.
items.quote: But next year, we'll be back, will be around 2.5%-3% ROA, what our target is for all of the businesses.

items.statement: Income-generating gold loans at 20% to 25% of book, may increase; started last quarter.
items.quote: I don't have a precise number, but I think about 20% to 25% will be income-generating loans as of now, and this might go up a little bit as we go along.

items.statement: Tax demand stayed; litigating, no further update.
items.quote: So there's no further update because there was assessment order, there was a tax demand. We've got stay on that, and we are litigating and we are presenting our case.

items.statement: Microfinance growth to pick up in second half with festival season momentum.
items.quote: And now I think the second half of the year, you can see a little more momentum building up during the festival season and there, we can see the momentum building up.

items.statement: DLF rental exit run rate expected at INR 175-180 crores quarterly, INR 750 crores annual.
items.quote: So, exit run rate, I would say, with full potential, it should be close to INR 175 -180 crores -- quarterly. So, on an annualized basis, close to INR 750 crores annual.

items.statement: DCCDL exit rental expected at INR 6,800 crores.
items.quote: So, the exit rental for DCCDL would be close to INR 6,800 crores, Parvez.

items.statement: Revenue inflection point expected in FY27-28, with INR 75,000 crores to be recognized over next few years.
items.quote: This we have highlighted earlier, that our inflection point of revenue, which is almost INR 75,000 crores of launched and projects so far, the inflection point you will see in FY'27-'28, and going forward next two/four/five years, is when this entire revenue is going to get recognized.

items.statement: Other expenses forward guidance to be in similar range as average of last two quarters.
items.quote: It will be in similar range. Average of last two quarters should be looked at for forward guidance as well.

items.statement: Other income expected at INR 150-200 crores on average.
items.quote: Apart from that, on an average, you will have almost INR150 to 200 crores of other income, which is interest income, interest from other subsidiaries, etcetera which will continue to happen.

items.statement: Dividend guidance continues to be annual.
items.quote: But now DLF dividend continues to be annual. We'll see in the future, but right now I think our guidance continues to be an annual dividend.

items.statement: DCCDL projects: Downtown Gurgaon, Mall of India Gurgaon, Downtown Chennai to be completed by fiscal 2030.
items.quote: So, DCCDL, we continue to keep on working on the balance office towers of Downtown , Gurgaon, the Mall of India, Gurgaon, and the Downtown, Chennai. And correct me, Navin and Badal, I think by and large, by fiscal '30, all of this should be done.

items.statement: Chennai Block 4 and 5 (3.6 million sq ft) to be operational by calendar next year.
items.quote: So on the Chennai 1, 2, 3 are already operational. Block 4 and 5 is what is under construction, which is together 3.6 million square feet, which will become operational by calendar next year.

items.statement: Downtown Gurgaon blocks 5,6,7,8 and MOIG completion targeted end of FY28 and FY29, operational between FY29 and FY30.
items.quote: And coming on to the Downtown Gurgaon, which is 5, 6, 7, 8 and the MOIG, the completion is targeted towards the end of FY28 and '29. So, most of the blocks will become operational between FY29 and '30.

items.statement: Goa project to be commissioned this fiscal; Chennai Block 3 and Building 7 next fiscal.
items.quote: Goa, Downtown Chennai, and Building 7 should all happen in the next -- and Goa this fiscal, and the balance two next fiscal.

items.statement: Dahlias price increased by almost 10% this time; further increase after Experience Centre.
items.quote: No. If you see this time's report, Dahlias has been seeing a price increase. In fact, it's already gone up by almost about 10% even this time. And the post the Experience Centre, once the show-and-tell begins, it's going to be there.

items.statement: Average realization per square feet was much ahead of INR 1,00,000 in this quarter.
items.quote: On a saleable, on an average, we were much ahead of INR 1,00,000 realization per square feet in this quarter. So, that price increase has been realizing and it has come a long way from the time when we had launched it.

items.statement: Strong demand for super-luxurious project Dahlias in current quarter.
items.quote: We continue to see absolutely strong demand for our super-luxurious project, Dahlias, in the current quarter as well.

items.statement: New luxury-plus project in DLF Phase 4 aimed for launch in Q4.
items.quote: So, that is not the name of the project. We are yet to name it. It's in the same vicinity, but it is going to be a luxury-plus product and we aim to launch it in Q4.

items.statement: Construction outflows may see slight blip in Q3 due to labor migration and GRAP guidelines, but no crisis foreseen.
items.quote: But you are right that last quarter, and possibly this quarter, could see a slight blip in construction outflows, primarily on two things. A, of course, is the fact that we are now entering the phase of chronic labor migration back for Chhath Puja and eve rything else that happens during this quarter, so traditionally.

items.statement: Targeting Housing.com profitability within 12 to 18 months; internal target 4-6 quarters, external 6-8 quarters.
items.quote: We are targeting to make Housing.com profitable within 12 to 18 months; I repeat, within 12 to 18 months.

items.statement: Expects revenue growth of INR100-150 crores over next 4-6 quarters to move Housing.com to profitability.
items.quote: We believe that there will be revenue growth of another INR100 crores, INR150 crores over next four to six quarters, which will kind of move Housing.com to profitability.

items.statement: KuberX loan disbursement run rate to scale from INR2,400 crores to INR25,000 crores in 4-6 quarters.
items.quote: So, this INR 2,400 odd crores of current run rate will, we believe, spiral up to INR 25,000 crores in next 4 quarters to 6 quarters.

items.statement: Revenue per team member to increase quarter-on-quarter for next 10-12 quarters.
items.quote: We believe revenue per team member will continue to go up quarter-on-quarter for next 10 to 12 quarters.

items.statement: Targets revenue per team member of INR56 lakhs by end of year, up from INR50-plus lakhs.
items.quote: Our target is to take this up to INR 56 lakhs by the end of the year.

items.statement: Rental team projects 88% occupancy by end of this year, up from 82%.
items.quote: now, on the network level, we are at 82% occupancy, and the team has projected it to be 88% occupancy by the end of this year.

items.statement: H1 capital expenditure mostly capitalized product development was INR8.8 crores.
items.quote: Capital expenditure, mostly capitalized product development was INR 8.8 crores, lease principal payments were INR 47.8 crores.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 adjusted EBITDA margins expanded 840 bps to 11.5%; PBT improved 1,270 bps to 4.8%.
items.quote: Adjusted EBITDA margins expanded 840 basis points to 11.5%. And while PBT improved 1,270 basis points to 4.8%.

items.statement: Q2 EBITDA was INR41 crores at 29.8% margin; H1 EBITDA INR78.5 crores at 30.6% margin.
items.quote: EBITDA was INR 41 crores a margin of 29.8% of total income.

items.statement: Cut approximately INR120 crores of costs at Housing.com within first week of acquisition.
items.quote: So within the first week of acquiring the business, we have cut costs of approximately INR120 crores on the business.

items.statement: Earns 1% to 1.2% commission from banks on home loan disbursals.
items.quote: we actually earn from the bank a commission between 1% to 1.2% of the disbursed value.

items.statement: Sees tailwinds as developers increase sales and marketing spend during slowdowns, benefiting platforms.
items.quote: in that phase, we typically see spending by real estate developers' increase on the sales and marketing budgets to attract new customers to bring in more demand, which is when the spending over platform companies like Aurum actually increases a lot.

items.statement: Plans to restart Housing.com's rental and education payments business with NestAway.
items.quote: we are actually planning to restart that business with Housing and NestAway together, and that will be a part of the synergies that we'll be launching going ahead.

items.statement: Housing.com comes with INR1,020 crores of carryforward losses; tax optimization still being evaluated.
items.quote: the carryforward loss that we have acquired is INR1,020 crores.

items.statement: H2 FY27 will be better than H1; FY27 growth endeavor to come close to FY26 growth.
items.quote: H2 will be better than H1. That is number one. Number two is that, FY27 overall year growth coming to the FY26, that is our endeavor.

items.statement: Q3 and Q4 will be better than Q1; FY2028 is the aim.
items.quote: I will hold on to that and say that Q3 and Q4 will be better quarters than the first quarter for sure, number one. And number two, FY2028, absolutely that is the aim.

items.statement: Working towards maintaining margin at similar levels to last year on consolidated basis.
items.quote: I think we had mentioned earlier that we are working towards maintaining our margin for this year at similar levels to previous year, and I think we are still working towards that.

items.statement: Organic margins expected to hold and improve further from here.
items.quote: So we do expect the organic margins to continue to hold on and improve further from here.

items.statement: AI rate cards priced higher than traditional rate cards; AI rate cards signed with customers.
items.quote: I mean, our AI rate cards are priced higher than the traditional rate cards. We actually created AI rate cards and got AI rate cards signed up with customers.

items.statement: Traditional large deals face pricing weakness; unit pricing going down in those areas.
items.quote: So, yes, in those areas, the more you hold on to those areas, the unit pricing is only going to go down.

items.statement: Growing demand across AI stack; AI primary driver of growth.
items.quote: As AI adoption accelerates, we are seeing a growing demand across the AI stack, reinforcing our conviction that AI will become foundational intelligence layer for modern enterprises and our primary driver of growth.

items.statement: Tech vertical to return to normal growth trajectory; good deals to realize revenue in Q3 and beyond.
items.quote: In fact, we will be back to the normal growth trajectory in the tech vertical. And we have got some good deals out there, which will start realizing revenue as we go into Q3 and beyond.

items.statement: Travel and hospitality customers expected to return budgets put on hold temporarily.
items.quote: So I expect them to come back and put all those budgets that were put on hold temporarily, into these new areas.

items.statement: AI revenue reached 13.4% of overall revenue, growing 40% year-over-year.
items.quote: AI revenue for the quarter has reached 13.4% of our overall revenue, a growth of 40% year-over-year.

items.statement: AI deals are short-tenured, faster revenue realization, incremental; majority of order inflow is ACV.
items.quote: The order inflow reflects AI-centric deals that are short-tenured, have a faster revenue realization, and are incremental in nature.

items.statement: Saudi business impact beyond control; demand outside Saudi is strong.
items.quote: The good news is that, we have a lot of demand elsewhere, right, outside of the Saudi, because the situation in Saudi is beyond our control.

items.statement: Traditional services will continue to be challenged; industry deflation to go on for a couple of years.
items.quote: But I would expect from an industry standpoint, this will go on for a couple of years.

items.statement: Board approved interim dividend of ₹25 per equity share, up 13.6% YoY.
items.quote: The Board of Directors has approved an interim dividend of ₹.25 per equity share, an increase of 13.6% from the corresponding quarter of the previous year.

items.statement: Randstad digital acquisition approvals expected in Q3; closure by end of Q3.
items.quote: Regarding our previously announced plan to acquire certain Randstad digital businesses in Europe and Australia, the approval process is on track, and we expect to receive all the approvals in Q3 as previously communicated.

items.statement: Cash conversion to normalize in Q3, except some gratuity funding may still occur.
items.quote: It will normalize in quarter three, except that to some extent, the gratuity funding may still be happening.

items.statement: Order book at quarter end was INR2,315 crores versus INR1,529 crores in Q1.
items.quote: And order book at the end of the quarter was INR2,315 crores while Q1 order book was INR1,529 crores.

items.statement: Most of the BSNL INR1,500 crores is expected to enter order book by end of this quarter.
items.quote: So all of INR1,500 crores is not there in the order book yet, but they will come -- most of it, we expect to come by the end of this quarter.

items.statement: Company targets achieving quarterly positive EBITDA performance.
items.quote: We'll have increased focus on collections. I mean a lot of the customer deliveries and commitments have been executed and also there will be a major focus on the customer receivables and achieving quarterly positive EBITDA performance.

items.statement: Company sees a visible path to profitability in the upcoming years.
items.quote: And we are also on the path of steadily improving our financial performance, and we have a visible path to profitability in the upcoming years.

items.statement: BSNL expansion order execution will significantly bring down inventory and gross debt.
items.quote: An important thing that's going to happen is the execution of the BSNL expansion order, which will bring down our inventory and gross debt significantly.

items.statement: Significant inventory reduction expected over next few quarters from BSNL expansion order execution.
items.quote: And so over the next few quarters, we certainly should see a significant reduction of this inventory. That's all I can say, right? And it will come down to much -- to the earlier levels, which are in line with the kind of quarterly business that we do.

items.statement: Significant debt reduction expected with shipments and collections.
items.quote: Again, from a debt point of view, we're going to see a significant reduction, right? And both of these, I kind of mentioned in my presentation in the financial outlook going forward, both inventory and debt is going to come down significantly with the order.

items.statement: Significant BSNL collections expected this quarter, substantially reducing receivables.
items.quote: And this is the quarter when we will see a significant amount of collections coming from BSNL, which are connected to the milestones that we have achieved. So I cannot specify the exact number, but it is going to substantially reduce our receivables.

items.statement: Company has strong business visibility for the next few quarters based on order book growth.
items.quote: And so the key takeaways for the quarter is that we have a strong growth in order book based on which we have strong business visibility for the next few quarters.

items.statement: Global 5G FWA subscriptions expected to triple and reach close to 90 million by 2030.
items.quote: The other important factor is the global 5G FWA subscriptions, the fixed wireless access are supposed to triple and reach close to 90 million by 2030.

items.statement: 5G rollouts in emerging markets expected to continue until 2030.
items.quote: So looking forward, some of the key business drivers in wireless continues to be the expansion of 5G deployment in emerging markets and the 5G rollouts, which are supposed to continue until 2030.

items.statement: Company expanding 5G radio portfolio to cover bands from 700 MHz to 4.9 GHz.
items.quote: These are all custom, and we are expanding our radio portfolio to cover all these bands as they go from 700 megahertz to 4.9 gigahertz.

items.statement: Developing compact baseband unit supporting up to 5 frequency bands in 1 site.
items.quote: We are also developing a compact baseband unit, which is as good as the best in the industry, which will support up to 5 frequency bands in 1 site.

items.statement: Developing high-capacity, low-latency access platforms at 200 gig and beyond.
items.quote: In the access, latency, low latency is becoming important, especially because of AI-based applications. And we are developing high-capacity, low-latency access platforms at 200 gig and beyond.

items.statement: Company filed 26 patents in Q2, taking global patent count to 748.
items.quote: We filed 26 patents in Q2, taking our global patent count to 748.

items.statement: Company is radio development partner for many of NEC's future radios.
items.quote: So we are part of the agreement that we are radio development partner for many of their future radios, and we are engaged in developing many of the new generation radio s for their customers in their international markets.

items.statement: Long-term gross margin guidance maintained at 32%.
items.quote: My guidance in the long run stays at about 32%, and that's what we are working.

items.statement: Expects to trend closer to double-digit EBITDA margin in next 4-6 quarters, especially H2 onwards.
items.quote: I see at some point in the next four to six quarters, at least in H2 onwards, you will see us trending far closer to that.

items.statement: Price increases of 3-6% taken in Q2 across categories, with additional ~3% in October.
items.quote: we've taken price increases of 3% to 6% across various categories in quarter two, and another increase of approximately 3% in October in some of the categories

items.statement: Price hikes have covered 80-100% of inflation depending on category.
items.quote: different category-wise it'll range from about 80% on, let's say, a fan, then appliances close to about 90%, wires closer to 100%, and rest of it would be in the range of 80% to 100% of what the inflation led.

items.statement: BLDC fans grew 26% YoY and now ~30% of ceiling fan portfolio.
items.quote: This quarter, we had 26% growth on BLDC. Almost 30% of our ceiling fan now comes on the BLDC portfolio.

items.statement: Premium products ~40% of fan mix; new products >30% of fan revenue.
items.quote: Premium products accounted for approximately 40% of the fan mix. Our focus on innovation and premiumization continues to yield encouraging results, with new products contributing more than 30% of the fans revenue during the quarter.

items.statement: Project Sanchay cost savings: INR13 crores in Q2, INR23 crores in H1; expect to cross last year's INR70 crores in H2.
items.quote: Our cost optimization program, Project Sanchay, continued to deliver results, generating savings of approximately INR13 crores during the quarter and approximately INR23 crores for H1 through focused cost initiatives.

items.statement: Working capital at 34 days; expect to reduce to ~20 days in next 4-6 quarters.
items.quote: We've moved our working capital 30, 34 days. In the next four to six quarters, it should come back to about 20 days, given the point that we're doing in terms of our channel financing and everything.

items.statement: Hyderabad facility at 40% utilization; expect 20-30 bps margin benefit at steady state.
items.quote: on a steady state, where inflation is not taking away the benefit, and the utilization going up, we should see about a 20, 30 basis point coming from Hyderabad utilization.

items.statement: Confident in outlook for H2 and festive season, with market share gains and new products.
items.quote: As we move through the festive season and the second half, we remain confident in our outlook, given the brand preference, market share gains, and a refreshed consumer-centric innovative portfolio of products across all three stages of the wall.

items.statement: Persistent commodity inflation in copper, aluminum, steel, plastics; no predictability on inflation.
items.quote: During the quarter, we continue to face persistent commodity inflation, particularly in copper and aluminum. Crude-linked movements added further pressure on raw material costs and, in turn, on our gross margins.

items.statement: R&D spend at 0.8-0.9% of turnover.
items.quote: In terms of our R&D spends, we do about 0.8% to 0.9% of our turnover.

items.statement: Added 3,000-4,000 outlets in fans distribution.
items.quote: on a large base of about 1 lakh plus direct and indirect distribution that we do on fans, we would have added about 3,000 to 4,000 more outlets.

items.statement: Expects NIM to be around 8.35% in H2 FY27 due to repo rate impact.
items.quote: So we feel the margin would come down to around 8.35% for the second half of the year.

items.statement: Micro banking loan growth guidance for FY27 is 12-14%.
items.quote: It would be somewhere between 12% to 14%, in between 12% to 14%.

items.statement: Secured book to reach 56% by end of FY27, improving 5% annually thereafter.
items.quote: Today, it is at 52%. We expect it to reach 56% by end of the year. And going forward every year 5% improvement.

items.statement: Opex to ATA ratio expected at 6.2% for FY27, lower than earlier 6.4%.
items.quote: Now considering the way it is moving, we feel it may end up at 6.2%. So there could be a saving of 0.2 opex to ATA ratio.

items.statement: Credit cost in H2 to be similar to H1, within guided range.
items.quote: As we said, credit cost in H2 is similar to the credit cost in H1.

items.statement: Likely to overshoot guided ROA range for FY27.
items.quote: Considering these outcomes, we could overshoot our guided ROA range.

items.statement: Raising INR409 crores equity from QIBs via preferential allotment.
items.quote: Within the shareholders approved resolution at the AGM, we propose to raise equity capital of INR409 crores from QIBs by issuing shares on a preferential basis to marquee investors, International Finance Corporation, Bajaj Life Insurance, HDFC Life Insurance, and Aditya Birla Sun Life Insurance, subject to shareholder approval.

items.statement: Balance fundraise up to INR2,000 crores planned before resolution expires in July 2027.
items.quote: You are aware we have approval for up to INR2,000 crores for the fundraise, out of which INR409 crores, we have got the approval today, and we'll be going ahead with it. Okay. Now as far as the balance is concerned, the resolution is valid up to July 2027.

items.statement: Cost of funds expected to increase by around 10 bps due to repo rate hike.
items.quote: And as you rightly mentioned, repo rate has gone up by 25 bps. So that will have an impact of around 10 bps on the margin.

items.statement: No rate hikes taken in Q2; calibrated rate revisions may occur as needed.
items.quote: Although no rate hikes were taken in Q2, the increase effective in Q1 would now start showing, and we expect the cost of funds to start moving upwards.

items.statement: Expects enhanced business momentum during festive season.
items.quote: We are geared up for the festive season and expect enhanced business momentum.

items.statement: Deficient monsoon and El Nino pose risk to rural demand.
items.quote: A deficient Southwest monsoon and strong El Nino conditions pose risk to rural demand, while urban demand remained stable.

items.statement: IRDAI consultation paper on insurance commissions; awaiting final guidelines.
items.quote: IRDAI's notification is a consultation paper, and we await the final guidelines on the matter. We remain engaged with our insurance partners as well as through IBA channels.

items.statement: Secured business lines now 52.1% of loan book, growing faster.
items.quote: The secured business lines continue to grow faster and now forms 52.1% of the loan book.

items.statement: MD succession process expected to complete in 3-4 months from September 1.
items.quote: And we hope to complete the process in around 3 to 4 months, starting September 1. So we should be able to complete it in 3 to 4 months.

items.statement: Expects FY27 EBITDA margin around 12% plus/minus, with improvement starting next year.
items.quote: So I think this year, we will be at similar kind of EBITDA of around 12% plus/minus. That is what for this year is our take.

items.statement: Full-year revenue growth expected mid-teen to slightly high-teen.
items.quote: But I think our initial assessment of 12%, 14%, I think we should do a between mid-teen to a little high-teen numbers for the year-end.

items.statement: Targets exports to be at least 30% plus of overall revenue by end of this year.
items.quote: So our first target, I think by the end of this year should be that at least 30% plus of our revenue should come from export and we have been working towards that.

items.statement: Remaining H2 FY27 capex of Rs 50-75 crore; no significant capex next year.
items.value: Rs. 50 crore to Rs. 70 crore, Rs. 75 crore
items.quote: I think we'll have another about between Rs. 50 crore to Rs. 70 crore, Rs. 75 crore of spend that will happen in the second half. And then I think nothing beyond that.

items.statement: New ethoxylation facility to reach peak utilization by end of FY28, targeting 3x capex as peak sales.
items.quote: So probably we'll have the peak utilization targets by end of FY28. And we still stick to the target of 3x of the CAPEX value to be the peak sales revenue.

items.statement: Reliance EO expansion expected in Q1 next financial year, enabling higher EO allocation.
items.quote: So we are expecting in the first quarter of next financial year for the Reliance expansion to kick in, and we should get higher amount of EO allocation from the first quarter

items.statement: Freight costs doubled/tripled YoY, compressing core B2B EBITDA margin; not all customers absorb increases.
items.quote: Even though our exports have grown significantly, the freight costs have almost doubled, tripled over what they were in the first half of last year or Q2 of last year. That has significantly impacted our EBITDA margins.

items.statement: Pharma, aroma segments to drive steady gross margin improvement once they scale, a few quarters away.
items.quote: as these segments like pharma, aroma, you know, start becoming a significant part of the overall business, we should see steady gross margin improvement, you know, going forward.

items.statement: Focus on higher-margin products; tail-cutting bottom 5% low-margin products improved gross and EBITDA margins.
items.quote: Tail cutting means with the bottom 5% of the products who have the least margins are cut off from the tail and we stop producing or selling those products.

items.statement: AHN Q2 is seasonally weakest; Q3 and Q4 will be peak season for Animal Health.
items.quote: Generally, the second quarter is the weakest for the AHN division. The third and fourth quarters will peak.

items.statement: B2C/institutional business targeted EBITDA positive in H2 and breakeven for full year.
items.quote: So our aim is that at least in the next two quarters, at least H2 should also be an EBITDA positive second half for us. And overall, on a full year basis, we should at least breakeven in this business

items.statement: All cash flows to go into debt reduction; working capital debt-free by mid next year.
items.quote: But yes, currently, all cash flows will go into debt reduction.

items.statement: Saudi Arabia greenfield project: land lease approved, next steps and timelines in 8-12 months.
items.quote: Hopefully some of these developments will happen over the next 8 months to 12 months.

items.statement: FY27 disbursements will surpass last year's disbursements; guidance remains intact.
items.quote: To answer your question in very clear manner, the guidance that we have given is that, in FY27 also, we will surpass disbursement that we did last FY, and that guidance remains intact.

items.statement: AUM target of near INR5,00,000 crores by end of FY27 is fully intact.
items.quote: So, as I mentioned to you, we stand by the target of reaching near about INR5,00,000 crores, maybe more than that, maybe 1,000 or 2,000 possible shortfall but the target is fully intact for end of FY27.

items.statement: PAT will grow nearly 10% as long as the diversification model continues.
items.quote: So, even if I'm maintaining the AUM size of INR5 lakh crores, you can rest be assured that my PAT will be growing nearly to 10% not for a year or 2, as long we continue with this mode.

items.statement: By 2030, mix will be 60% pure Railways and 40% diversification.
items.quote: Given the way we have forecasted that by 2030, our mix will be 60% pure Railways and 40% will be diversification, rest assured that till 2030 there is no look ing back.

items.statement: Railway pipeline includes DFC, seven high-speed corridors, and six freight lines, totaling over INR20 lakh crores.
items.quote: There are seven high-speed rail corridors that have already been sanctioned and very actively being pursued, because country is moving towards Viksit Bharat. Railways has also announced six freight lines where they will be going on JV, joint venture model or PPP model. So overall, pie that comes out to be more than INR20 lakh crores.

items.statement: From FY28 onwards, minimum INR50,000 crores per year expected from Indian Railways for a decade.
items.quote: That pie will be going forward, maybe from FY28 onwards for next decade, minimum 50,000 crores every year coming from the Indian Railways.

items.statement: H2 lending pipeline includes metros, ports, renewable energy, thermal power, Gencos, and road linkages, ready for Q3 or early Q4 disbursement.
items.quote: Next, in H2, you will find that we will be lending to metros, ports, renewable energy, thermal power, Gencos that have linkages with the Railways. We will be lending to few road linkages also. These are all in pipeline and are, almost ready to be disbursed in Q3 or early Q4.

items.statement: Non-IR business margins are at least 2 to 3.5 times higher than Railways margins.
items.value: 2 times or 3 times and 3.5 times high
items.quote: Now. You look at the beautiful and sweet spot for this company. Whatever non-IR business that we are garnering, margin is atleast 2 times or 3 times and 3.5 times high.

items.statement: Minimum margin of INR0.90 or INR0.85 targeted for non-railway business.
items.quote: In every scenario, strategy we have followed is that we must make at least a margin of INR0.90 or INR0.85 minimum.

items.statement: WACC of 6.55% maintained, with plans to reduce via 54EC bonds and ECB.
items.quote: We are very actively looking at reducing our WACC by increasing the share of 54EC bonds and also ECB, so that borrowing costs are least cost amongst other NBFCs and we hope to continue the same thing. We hope to continue in the same way, because at the moment 6.55% is our WACC which is much lower compared to other NBFCs.

items.statement: Yen borrowing cost landed at 2.25% despite TONAR increase; hedging cost not crossed 6.3%.
items.quote: In terms of yen consumption, last year we raised nearly USD2 billion worth of dollars. We started with 1.8%, with TONAR increase also we are landing somewhere at 2.25%.

items.statement: No prepayment pressure due to no prepayment penalty, no floor price, and cheapest market rates.
items.quote: Number one, there is no prepayment penalty. Listen to it very carefully. My first proposition to all my prospective borrowers that, we are not putting any prepayment penalty, whereas others, as you know better than I do, what kind of penalty is being put on Number two, we are saying that there is no floor price.

items.statement: H2 FY27 performance expected to replicate H1 FY27 numbers.
items.quote: I think I've spoken enough with all clarity. So nothing more to add, just to sum up that the way we are giving out the numbers that's come out in this FY for H1, we very seriously believe that this growth story will continue, and the numbers that we have shown in H1 will be kind of replica of what is going to be in H2.

items.statement: AUM will be better than last year.
items.quote: As for our AUM we are all geared up that we'll be doing better than what we did last year.

items.statement: ROCE grew nearly 14% and ROTA near 5% in H1.
items.quote: And all ratios that people follow, we believe that the way ROCE of this company in this H1 to H1 has grown in double digit, nearly 14%. Even ROTA has also grown near 5%.

items.statement: Bank of America agreed to acquire 49.9% stake in Jio Credit, expected to bring around Rs. 18,000 crore growth capital.
items.quote: In our lending vertical, we struck a landmark partnership during the quarter with Bank of America agreeing to acquire a 49.9% stake in Jio Credit. The transaction, which is subject to regulatory approvals, is expected to bring around Rs. 18,000 crore in growth capital.

items.statement: First tranche of Bank of America investment of around Rs. 9,500 crore into Jio Credit, subject to approvals, will bolster capital base.
items.quote: The infusion of the first tranche of its investment of around Rs. 9,500 crore from Bank of America into Jio Credit Limited, subject to regulatory and statutory approvals, will further bolster our capital base and strengthen our balance sheet for long-term expansion.

items.statement: Jio Payment Solutions deliberately pivoted to margin-accretive merchant segments, causing planned churn in lower-margin segments.
items.quote: The quarter-on-quarter adjustment in TPV was a deliberate outcome of our strategic pivot 2 towards margin-accretive merchant segments. While this focus led to planned customer churn in lower-margin segments, it helped us realise higher net processing margins, giving us a base to grow volumes further with strong unit

items.statement: Net processing margin rose to 14 basis points in Q2 FY27 from 9 bps in Q2 FY26 and 12 bps in Q1 FY27.
items.quote: Our net processing margin increased to 14 basis points in Q2 FY27, up from 9 basis points in Q2 FY26 and 12 basis points in Q1 FY27.

items.statement: Average cost of borrowing excluding TREPS was 7.08% in Q2 FY27 versus 7.07% in Q1 FY27.
items.quote: Our average cost of borrowing, excluding TREPS, stood at 7.08% in Q2 FY27, compared to 7.07% in Q1 FY27, demonstrating strong stability in a dynamic interest rate environment.

items.statement: Over 70% of AUM is on floating rates, allowing interest rate adjustments to be passed to borrowers with minimal lag.
items.quote: On interest rate risk management, over 70% of our Assets Under Management are on floating rates, enabling interest rate adjustments to be seamlessly passed on to borrowers with minimal time lag.

items.statement: Jio Payment Solutions chose to let go of certain high-volume, low-margin engagements, focusing on profitable growth over volume expansion.
items.quote: Consequently, we chose to let go of certain high-volume, low-margin engagements, as our focus remains firmly on profitable growth rather than volume expansion alone.

items.statement: Jio Payment Solutions is actively pursuing high-margin segments including small and medium businesses and exporters.
items.quote: To drive profitable growth, we are actively pursuing high-margin segments, including small and medium businesses as well as exporters.

items.statement: IRDAI draft insurance distribution regulations may reshape the industry and lead to consolidation; Jio Insurance Broking will recalibrate strategy based on final rules.
items.quote: We view this as a significant regulatory shift that will reshape the industry landscape and may lead to consolidation. However, larger, well-capitalized, and technology-driven players like Jio Insurance Broking should be able to strengthen their presence, also benefiting from being part of a larger and integrated financial services ecosystem.

items.statement: Primary insurers recalibrated crop insurance exposure to align with seasonal and environmental factors, moderating sequential reinsurance volume.
items.quote: Primary insurance carriers recalibrated their exposure to crop insurance to align with seasonal and environmental factors, which moderated sequential volume.

items.statement: Jio Credit AUM mix: mortgages 44.5%, corporate and SME loans 44.2%, retail LAS 11.3%.
items.quote: Mortgages, comprising Home Loans and Loan Against Property, account for 44.5% of the total portfolio, with an average ticket size of Rs. 1.4 crore and an average tenor of 15.9 years.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 disbursement mix: mortgages 26.1%, Loan Against Securities 20%, corporate and SME loans 53.9%.
items.quote: In terms of the disbursement mix for Q2 FY27, Mortgages contributed 26.1%, Loan Against Securities represented 20%, and Corporate and SME Loans accounted for 53.9%.

items.statement: Jio Payments Bank received regulatory approvals to launch 3-in-1 Savings Account and act as Banker to the Issue for public offerings including IPOs.
items.quote: During the quarter, we also received key regulatory approvals to launch our 3-in-1 Savings Account as well as to act as ‘Banker to the Issue’ for public offerings, including IPOs, which will open up new revenue streams for the payments bank.

items.statement: Jio Allianz General Insurance is in advanced stages for regulatory approvals to commence operations.
items.quote: In general and health insurance, Jio Allianz General Insurance Limited is in advanced stages for securing regulatory approvals to commence operations.

items.statement: GIFT City entity received IFSCA approval to launch BlackRock Advantage World Equity Fund, planned for launch during the current quarter.
items.quote: Finally, another important milestone during the quarter was our GIFT City entity receiving regulatory approval from the IFSCA to launch the BlackRock Advantage World Equity Fund. The fund planned for launch during the current quarter, opens up global investment pipelines for Indian investors.

items.statement: JioBlackRock AMC partnered with over 15,000 mutual fund and SIF distributors and launched Regular Plans across all product offerings.
items.quote: As highlighted in our distribution strategy, we have now partnered with over 15,000 Mutual Fund and Specialized Investment Fund distributors, and have launched Regular Plans across all our product offerings to complement our Direct Plans.

items.statement: AUM growth guidance of 20-25% for the year, assuming flat gold prices.
items.quote: We will continue to give the same guidance in spite of the gold prices being almost flat. So we will give a AUM growth of about 20% to 25% for the year.

items.statement: Targeting 3% ROA and 18% ROE.
items.quote: Our target ROA we are trying to reach is 3% and correspondingly try and touch an 18% ROE.

items.statement: Credit cost to remain below 1%.
items.quote: This guidance that we have given is the credit cost that w e will manage will be way below 1%.

items.statement: GNPA to remain below 2%.
items.quote: If you remember last year as well as the start of the year, I told you that the GNPAs will also be below 2%.

items.statement: Plan to add at least 150 branches in H2 FY27.
items.quote: In addition to the 74 branches we added in quarter 2, we propose to add at least another 150 branches in the second half of the year.

items.statement: Expects better performance in H2 due to seasonality.
items.quote: Historically, the second half of the year is a much stronger period for us, which is giving us confidence that in spite of the headwinds you mentioned, we would be able to perform to our guidance, which we have been giving in the earlier quarters for this year on AUM growth.

items.statement: Small ticket LAP disbursals to be best in last 8-9 quarters in Q3.
items.quote: I can't give you a definite guidance, but I can tell you so much that it will be amongst the last 8 or 9 quarters, it will be the best quarter compared to the last 8 or 9 quarters.

items.statement: Yield trajectory to improve in Q3 for small ticket LAP.
items.quote: But you will definitely see a different yield trajectory i n Q3. Definitely, it will be more than Q2 as well as the disbursals will be more.

items.statement: Tonnage growth to improve in H2.
items.quote: So you will see a different trajectory in H2 for tonnage.

items.statement: Will use multiple levers to manage yields and ROA.
items.quote: As far as the yield is concerned, - for Q3 and Q4, we will use all levers possible, whether it is yield, whether it is LTV and growth, it will be a combination.

items.statement: Stage II and III increases are technical, not credit concerns.
items.quote: As far as the gold piece is concerned, this Stage II is technical in nature. You are aware, most of the gold loan product is a 3 -month or 2.5 -month behavioural tenor product. So this will not translate into a credit cost.

items.statement: Branch profitability at INR6-7 crores AUM in 12-13 months.
items.quote: Typically, a branch, if it reaches about INR6 crores to INR7 crores of AUM, it turns profitable for us. when the price is going on an upward trajectory or even the price that is there today, in 12 to 13 months, the branch starts touching that number.

items.statement: Approval rates for ST LAP improved to mid-40%.
items.quote: So approval rates for earlier when we were coming out of the woods had dropped down to about 30% levels. Now steadily, they have moved up to the mid-40% or the early 40% levels.

items.statement: Insurance income contribution to ROA is about 0.1%.
items.quote: So, from an ROA tree perspective, I would put the number at about 0.1% in the ROA tree from an income perspective, a little over 0.1%.

items.statement: Expects Q3 and Q4 volumes stronger than Q2; H2 typically 20% higher than H1.
items.quote: Based on our current indication, we expect Q3 and Q4 volumes to be stronger than Q2. Overall volumes and historically also H2 is always 20% up on H1.

items.statement: Exports expected to be 45% higher this year than previous year.
items.quote: Year-on-year, we expect this year to be 45% higher than our previous year.

items.statement: Seamless tube facility production trials planned for February or March 2027.
items.quote: The sizing mill and straightening mills have been received and installed, and we plan to undertake production trials in February or March of 2027.

items.statement: Total seamless tube capex budget INR170 crores; INR120 crores spent as of Q2.
items.quote: the total budgeted cost is approximately INR170 crores, okay? Out of this is funded by INR110 crores via term loan. The rest is from internal accruals, okay?

items.statement: Plans INR60 crores immediate capex via warrants and pref shares over next two quarters.
items.quote: close to INR60 crores we are planning on an immediate capex via warrants and pref shares, which we would be spending between the next 2 quarters.

items.statement: Further INR50 crores capex on seamless tube in H2; total H2 capex about INR110 crores.
items.quote: we are looking at a further balanced capex of close to INR50-odd crores out of the INR170 crores, which is there.

items.statement: Backward integration into seamless tubes expected to add 3-4% margin on overall business.
items.quote: on the overall business, we should be having a margin of approximately 3% to 4% once we use our own seamless tubes for it.

items.statement: Seamless tube cost expected 8-10% lower than existing buying prices.
items.quote: it should be at around approximately 8% to 10% lesser than -- or you could say more competitive than existing buying prices.

items.statement: Price revisions with OEMs and Tier 1 customers to support Q3 and Q4.
items.quote: the price revisions, including -- concluded with the OEMs and Tier 1 customers are expected to support us during the Q3 and Q4.

items.statement: Steel prices increasing each quarter; OEMs and mills discussing another increase in Q3.
items.quote: steel as a commodity, we see increase going on in each and every quarter. I do believe that OEMs and mills are also talking about another increase in quarter 3 as well.

items.statement: Agri segment momentum to continue in Q3; tractor production planned at 13,000-14,000 in Oct-Nov.
items.quote: We expect this momentum to continue into Q3, supported by relatively lower inventory levels of tractors in the market.

items.statement: Extruded axle beam production at 80% of current output; to reach 100% by Q3 or Q4.
items.quote: Commercial production of our extruded axle beam has commenced and the capacity utilization of this is approximately 80% of our current output.

items.statement: Preferential issue of INR63.6 crores to fund expansion initiatives.
items.quote: The company is completely focused on capacity expansion and gearing up for the coming years, which is also witnessed by a preferential issue to the tune of INR63.6 crores.

items.statement: Difficult to guide on return to 14-15% EBITDA margins due to cost escalation and settlement pressures.
items.quote: Yes, it is difficult currently. The companies are facing a lot of pressures in terms of escalation and then the settlements and everything.

items.statement: H2 FY27 EBITDA growth expected in mid-to-high teens, with FY27 better than initial guidance.
items.quote: So we expect a very strong closing for the year and we definitely stay true on the guidance, that yes, H1 has been far stronger than the guidance and we expect the trends to continue but definitely mid-to-high teens (EBITDA) for the balance of the year is something that we are anchored towards.

items.statement: Q3 FY27 RevPAR growth expected in double digits.
items.quote: We see a lot of pick up happening around the long festive weekends that are there in the months of October and November. So we are very much on track for double -digit growth in terms of RevPAR in Q3 as well.

items.statement: Effective tax rate anticipated to be in the 20s in FY27.
items.quote: We anticipate an effective tax rate to be in 20s in FY27.

items.statement: Capex for five contracted pipeline hotels is around INR 1,432 crores, with INR 150 crores spent.
items.quote: So, I'll tell you the capex for our five contracted pipelines, is Agra, Srinagar, Ayodhya, Ranthambore, Bandhavgarh is around INR1,432 crores. We have spent around INR150 crores.

items.statement: Planned capex spending: around INR 450 crores by end of this year, INR 600 crores next year.
items.quote: By the end of this year, we will be spending around INR450 crores. Next year, we are looking at spending around INR600 crores, and subsequent to that, the balance capex.

items.statement: Mumbai BKC project capex remains INR 800 crores, split equally between equity and debt.
items.quote: There is no change in the overall capex cost as of now. The INR 800 crores of our committed capex remains the same; INR 400 crores of equity and INR 400 crores of debt.

items.statement: Contracted to over 5,200 keys by FY30, with about 2,600 under ownership.
items.quote: Our goal currently, we are already contracted, and at various, including our openings that we are at various stages of development, at over 5,200 keys by FY30, and which will include 2,600 or so keys, which will be under our ownership.

items.statement: Excluding ESOP and Coorg, flow-through was around 60% for the quarter.
items.quote: Excluding the ESOP cost, the EBITDA margin will be even better. The flow-through, excluding ESOP and exclud ing Coorg because Coorg is also stabilizing and it's not giving the EBITDA numbers as Jaipur and Udaipur, flow-through would be around 60% for the quarter.

items.statement: Management fees flow down to 85% to 90% into EBITDA for new managed openings.
items.quote: So, yes, for a new managed opening, if you get a management fees, it flows down to 85% to 90% into the EBITDA.

items.statement: Corporate rate negotiations targeting mid-to-high double-digit growth for CY27.
items.quote: So we are pitching for mid -to-high double-digit growth rates in terms of our ask rates , but the negotiations are on.

items.statement: International business grew low double-digit last quarter, expecting return to 50-50 mix.
items.quote: International business has also started slowly trickling in. In the last quarter, there was a low double-digit growth in terms of international business (even excluding BRICS).

items.statement: Suite occupancy rose over 700 basis points, with paid suite occupancy in mid-40s.
items.quote: If you look at our portfolio, our suite occupancy has risen by over 700 basis points. That shows you how our guests are willing to pay for experience and quality.

items.statement: Dubai asset operating at breakeven EBITDA, with renovation planned for early FY28.
items.quote: We are looking at taking the hotel under renovation in early '27, I would say probably early FY28, to be precise, like April or so is when we to start the renovating hotel, and finish the renovation within a year.

items.statement: Seeking shareholder approval for incremental fund infusion to buy FSI for BKC project.
items.quote: Since this is a material transaction with a related party, with the JV entity, Leela will shortly reach out to the shareholders for an approval of investment.

items.statement: Borrowing costs reduced by 30 basis points from mid-October through lender renegotiation.
items.quote: Additionally, our borrowing costs have reduced by a further 30 basis points from mid -October, as we have actively renegotiated with our lenders, which provides a shield from potential transmission of policy rate hikes.
